cells.act: carry it without tightening around it
cells.ask: When someone close to you is carrying something hard, sit with them and keep your own weight separate from theirs. Don't reach in to fix it or take it over. Notice whether the two stay apart.
cells.core:
You can sit with someone's hard thing without it becoming yours. Beside what is still growing, that is the whole work: the person stays a person, you stay yourself, and something loosens because nobody is gripping. They feel met, not absorbed.

Nothing here needs building. It needs one turn: when someone near you is carrying something, stay with them and don't reach in to fix or take it over. Hold your own ground beside theirs for the length of the conversation. That isn't distance — you're in it. But they keep their own shape, which is what they came for, and you walk away with yours. Do it once and the difference is plain.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel with someone and stay your own size.
cells.verb: feeling with someone rather than only about them
cells.place: in the care of what is still growing

cells.tense: You are bracing for a moment that hasn't arrived, and nothing between you and another person has an edge yet.
cells.act: let the thing end that is already over
cells.ask: Find one worry about someone you tend whose moment has already passed — you have carried it past anything it could teach. Say to yourself that it is finished, and let a day go by without touching it again.
cells.core:
Beside what is still growing, you run ahead of it. You feel the person's next worry before they do, pick it up, and carry a future that hasn't happened. That isn't care anymore — it's fused. You can't tell whose ache is whose, or whose problem is getting solved. Nothing that's growing has room while you're standing in its future.

So let one thing be over. There's a fear about someone you've held well past its usefulness. Find it. Declare it done, even if only inside your own head, and go a full day without reopening it. That's enough to feel the shift — the person across from you can breathe, and so can you. The rest tend to go quiet once the first one does.

cells.tense: You were at the door once with someone on the other side, and you didn't go through.
cells.act: adjust one dial a little, then stop
cells.ask: With someone you tend, change a single thing next time — ask a real question, or let a pause sit, or answer instead of letting it pass. Then stop. Don't reach for warmth. Let the change stand by itself.
cells.core:
Beside what is still growing, the care has gone quiet. You do the practical parts — you show up, you handle it, you make sure it's fine — and inside that, you aren't really there with the person. Warmth comes toward you and lands on a flat surface. That isn't coldness. Staying close just stopped feeling like something you do.

Adjust the dial once and it starts moving. There's a moment with someone you care for where you could ask a real question, or wait an extra beat, or answer rather than letting it pass. Change one of those — just one — and then stop. Don't try to warm the whole thing. You aren't chasing a feeling right away; you're finding out that the dial can move at all, and that the room shifts when it does.

cells.tense: You are standing in a room you are already writing in, without the pen.
cells.act: trace the pattern across the last few times
cells.ask: Think of three recent times you tended someone and they left steadier. Write one line for each that says plainly what you did. Then put it down without changing anything.
cells.core:
People leave your company steadier than they arrived. You don't notice it happening, and if someone handed it back to you, you'd say that was circumstance, or them, or nothing in particular. Meanwhile your hand is in it. The care is running and doing real work; it just doesn't come back to you as something you did. The ones close to you see it plainly.

Here's the way back in: look at three recent times you were with someone you tend and they walked away lighter. Write a line for each — what actually happened, said plainly. Don't change anything, don't try to improve it. You're putting your own hand back on paper you already signed. See the move once, and it belongs to you again.
cells.sheetLine: The care is yours. You just didn't sign it.
